findings.title: Delete (and Pause) never render in the list view even though their abilities are computed from promRule
findings.body: canDelete is now computed from the Grafana promRule abilities, but the Delete item is rendered only under `canDelete && rulerRule`. The list view no longer passes rulerRule (GrafanaRuleListItem passes only promRule), so Delete never appears in the list-view menu. Pause has the same gating on line 123 (`rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`), so Pause also disappears. Before this PR both were available in the list view, and the new promRule-based ability code for them is effectively dead. The GrafanaGroupLoader test asserts exactly 4 menu items (silence, copy link, duplicate, export), which locks in the missing Delete/Pause instead of catching the regression.

findings.title: Silence notifications menu item is a no-op in the list view
findings.body: In the list view AlertRuleMenu now shows 'Silence notifications' when the Grafana promRule silence ability is true, and its handler `handleSilence` sets showSilenceDrawer=true. But the drawer is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, and `rule` (the ruler DTO) is always undefined in the list view after this PR. Clicking Silence therefore sets state and nothing appears. No test clicks this item, so the gap is not caught.

findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered in a list without a key
findings.body: The grafana branch of the switch now renders <GrafanaRuleListItem> without a key prop, while the datasource and unknown branches still use key={key}. React emits 'unique key' warnings for this list. The component comment explicitly says the keys exist to prevent duplicates, so the removal looks accidental. Since rules are append-only today the visible impact is small, but row-level state is then keyed by index.

findings.title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously derived isFederated from isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) (source_tenants). It now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false` with a TODO. Federated groups therefore lose the immutability guard, so Update/Delete/Pause/DeletePermanently can be enabled for them. The isFederatedRuleGroup import was also dropped. This affects every caller of useAlertRuleAbility/useAlertRuleAbilities, not only the list view.

findings.title: Duplicate is offered for data-source rules via the Grafana-side fallback, bypassing ruler and datasource permission checks
findings.body: For non-Grafana rules AlertRuleMenu passes skipToken to useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities. With an undefined rule, useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities sets Duplicate to [AlwaysSupported, hasPermission(AlertingRuleCreate)] (useAbilities.ts line 318). canDuplicate ORs this with the ruler result, so Duplicate is shown for datasource-managed rules whenever the user holds the Grafana-wide create permission. This bypasses the ruler-availability check (duplicateSupported = isRulerAvailable) and the isPluginProvided check, and ignores the datasource's own write permission (AlertingRuleExternalWrite). The other OR'd actions (Edit, Delete, Silence, Export, Pause) are false on this path, so Duplicate is the only leak.

findings.title: Rule view link drops the returnTo parameter
findings.body: The previous GrafanaRuleLoader built the view href with `createRelativeUrl(..., { returnTo })` using createReturnTo(). The new GrafanaRuleListItem silently drops returnTo, so navigating from the list to the rule view and back no longer returns to the list context. This is unrelated to removing the ruler and appears accidental.

findings.title: Every list row now evaluates both ruler and Grafana ability hooks, duplicating folder and silence-config subscriptions
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu (and RuleActionsButtons.V2 the same way) now calls useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities for each row. Each full evaluation calls useFolder, the Grafana alerting-config RTK query, and folder permission lookups. For Grafana rows the ruler evaluation runs with an undefined rule and contributes nothing useful, so each row ends up with about four full ability evaluations. The hook comment already warns about ~80 rows on the list page. Only the applicable hook should be invoked per row.

findings.title: Doc comments still describe the removed ruler request
findings.body: The component docstring says it loads 'from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints', and the expectedRulesCount prop doc (line 19) says the ruler response may contain a different number of rules. After this change the component uses only the Prometheus endpoint, so both comments are wrong.
